observation.visible_scene: Top-down close view of a dark cooking pan whose left interior shows a bright brushed-metal sheen. A rectangular, pale-yellow stick of butter rests diagonally in the center, sitting in a pool of already-melted, foaming butter/oil that bubbles most visibly on the right side of the stick.
visible_changes: The solid stick of butter keeps essentially the same diagonal position, orientation and shape from the first to the last frame; no translation or rotation of the stick is evident.

The surrounding liquid pool and its foamy edge expand slightly outward over the segment: the dark left boundary of the melted pool creeps a little farther left, and the bubbly foam on the right grows marginally wider and shifts its bubble pattern.
The foam/bubbles on the right of the stick continuously rearrange and churn in place, indicating ongoing melting/boiling at the edges rather than a one-time event.
The bright metallic reflection on the pan's left wall stays fixed in position, suggesting the camera is stationary and the changes are physical (melting/spreading), not camera motion.
outside_clip_unknowns: The state of the pan and butter before any melting began (the pool is already present at t=0, so the onset is outside this excerpt).
Whether the stick eventually fully melts or the pan is later used for cooking — outcomes beyond the last frame are not shown.
uncertain_details: Any measurable shrinkage of the solid stick is too small to confirm within this ~2.7 s window.
Exact material of the pan (carbon steel / cast iron / non-stick) cannot be determined from appearance alone.
Camera motion is uncertain but background evidence (fixed metal highlight) supports a static viewpoint.
